newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds stall pre-US data, Brazil debt suffers.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds stall pre-US data, Brazil debt suffers.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mixed on Tuesday ahead of potentially trend-setting U.S. retail sales at 0830 EST/1230 GMT, although Brazilian Bradys were stung by a flurry of sell orders, traders said.
Political concerns were dominating the Brazil Brady market but this close to the U.S. data many players were on hold.

"If it is a fairly benign set of (U.S.) figures then attention will immediately turn to the PPI (producer price index) and CPI (consumer price index)," said an emerging market source at a European bank. The April PPI report is due out on Wednesday and the CPI for the same month is due out on Thursday. Dollar denominated debt has generally been helped by speculation the Federal Reserve may hold off on another interest rate increase for a while.
Economists polled by Reuters, on average, forecast retail sales fell 0.3 percent during the month of April and rose 0.1 percent with autos excluded.

"The market is expecting a fall in the headline figure and a rise in the core excluding autos but like last month the market will not be just focusing on the actual front number but any possiblility of backward revisions," an analyst said.

Among Latin Brady instruments, Brazilian Brady bonds suffered the biggest losses amid political concerns regarding the re-election amendment which would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term.
There was talk in the market of local press reports which criticised Cardoso's re-election campaign.

Brazilian C' bonds were 5/8 lower in London at 76-3/8 but fell as much as one percentage point earlier. The country's par bonds were 5/8 weaker at 64-1/8 bid and discount bonds were 7/8 lower at 80-1/2 bid.
The re-election bill is due to be studied and possibly voted on by the Senate's Constititional and Justice Committee later this week.

The bill has already been approved once in the committee but was sent back after four amendments were proposed on the Senate floor. One of those amendments would force state governors seeking re-election to stand down from office for six months prior to election day.
The re-election proposal is reported to have the backing of about half the Senate's 81 members who intend to stand as state governors next year.
Among Eastern European Bradies, prices were mixed with Bulgarian IABs down 1/4 at 65-1/2 bid and POland discount bonds up 1/8 at 98-1/2 bid.
